title: From the CS-80 to the Deckard’s Dream
intro: The Deckard’s Dream is Black Corporation’s analogue polysynth built around the Yamaha CS-80’s voice. Its name points to Blade Runner, whose score Vangelis played on a CS-80. Its maker calls it not a clone but a revival of the CS-80’s sound design: the same two layers per note, IL-AL-A-D-R filter envelope and sine past the filters, in a keyless module played over MIDI with polyphonic aftertouch.

timeline.name: Yamaha CS-80
timeline.text: Yamaha’s eight-voice flagship: two channels per note, each a VCO, high-pass and low-pass filters with the IL-AL-A-D-R envelope and a VCA, a keyboard that senses velocity and pressure on each key, a ribbon, a ring modulator and a tremolo/chorus. About 100 kg.

timeline.name: Black Corporation Deckard’s Dream
timeline.text: The CS-80’s voice without the keyboard, ribbon, ring modulator or chorus, as an eight-voice module with two layers per voice, 16 VCOs, stored presets, MIDI with polyphonic aftertouch and MPE, and an external input for the sub oscillator. Sold built or as a kit; a separate Expander added ring modulation, chorus and a master sustain.

timeline.name: Black Corporation Deckard’s Dream MK2
timeline.text: A slimmer, lighter version with the same engine, adding the master SUSTAIN slider, the SUSTAIN I/II switch and a PANEL button, with sample and hold in place of the external input.

relatives.name: Yamaha CS-80
relatives.text: The synth it is modelled on, in the app beside it: switch between the two from the version toggle.

relatives.name: Black Corporation Kijimi
relatives.text: Black Corporation’s other eight-voice analogue polysynth in the same rack-style case, inspired by the RSF PolyKobol II.

relatives.name: Behringer DS-80
relatives.text: Behringer’s planned copy of the CS-80, first mentioned in 2020 and not on sale.

note: Which records used a Deckard’s Dream is rarely documented, so no players are listed. Where a sound credits Vangelis, it is the CS-80 sound he made, which the Deckard’s Dream was built to revive.
